lessons.title: Course Material: Checklist-1 (3).pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1 Strategic Website Content – Summary Checklist  Introduction – Determining the Key Pages for Your Website  ü The key question is ‘What do you want your visitors to do?’ ü Start with your end goal in mind ü You need to clarify: o Who are you? o What are you offering? o What CTA do you want to create? o Where did your visitor come from? o What does your visitor need? ü You can segment your site according to customer groups ü You can organize by topic ü You can organize according to where they have come from ü Prioritize content and decide where it goes  Home Page ü The home page directs the visitor to all of your website's other pages ü It serves as a portal to everything else your site has to offer

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2 About Us ü Your About Us page is where your customer gets to know more about your business ü The About Us page may also link to other sites, social media, etc.  Start Here Page ü The Start Here Page is a place to start in exploring your website ü Present to them here the first information they need to know about you and your site  Blog Page ü Your blog is your online journal ü Users can search for specific information using keywords  Learning Objectives: ü Key pages you need ü How to identify and incorporate the most important components ü How to produce an About Us page that tells your story ü The importance of the Start Here page ü The value of a well-designed blog page ü Other pages you need ü Best practices ü How to create a personalized action plan

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3 Action Steps: 1. List the primary goals of your website. Who are you? What do you offer? 2. Write an overview of the information you feel is needed in your website content. What does your user need? What are they looking for?  How do you fill that need?

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4 Module 1 - Create a First-Rate Home Page  ü Your home page tells visitors who you are, what you do and what you have to offer ü It should address questions and problems ü Show solutions ü Start with the goal you have in mind for the site ü Put yourself in your visitor’s shoes o Who is this? o What do they do? o What makes them different? o What else do they have to offer? ü Content should answer these basic questions  Elements of a Good Home Page ü It’s compelling and makes visitors want to stay and interact ü It’s clear and speaks to expectations ü It is well organized and easy to take in ü Navigation is clear ü It should be dynamic and include news and updates ü Fresh content also helps with SEO

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5 The Essential Components of a Good Home Page A headline that says who you are ü Explain succinctly and clearly who you are and what you do  Visuals ü It's good to include at least one visual that relates to your business or products  Bullet-point list of benefits ü These should explain the positive improvement in the visitor's life that your website and/or its products provide  Call to Action ü The call to action tells the visitor what they must do in order to receive the listed benefits  Introduction to other pages ü Explain how each page will help them by speaking to their needs  Additional Optional Components for Your Home Page Content Offer ü Some kind of freebie to download  Social Proof ü Testimonials or reviews

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6 Content for Your Home Page ü Content should be brief ü Make it personal to connect with the reader ü Break up text into small paragraphs ü Use keywords in a natural way ü Always proofread all content ü Make a good first impression    Action Steps: 1. Analyze your current Home Page and what it should be saying about your business and services. Based on the module, what is missing, or needs to be added or enhanced? 2. Based on your analysis in step one, draft content for your Home Page using the key points from the module and your business’s keywords and keyword phrases.

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7 Module 2 - Design Your Captivating About Us Page  ü The About Us page starts building a relationship with visitors ü They’re looking for information and similar values ü Along with the Home page, it’s the most visited page  Creating Your About Page Content ü Tell the visitor about you ü Make it personal and tell a story ü Don’t get into product or service specifics ü Present facts about your business but don’t be promotional ü Some things to include: o When/where did the company start? o Is it family owned? o Who runs it? ü Answer questions from the visitors POV ü Place the most important information at the top ü Include (real) graphics or pictures ü Include social media links ü Update news regularly ü Make sure all info is relevant and interesting

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8 Further Tips on About Us Page Content ü Use SEO Keywords ü Be concise ü Add a contact link    Action Steps: 1. Define what story you want to tell about your company. List your mission, goals, and product benefits. 2. Analyze your current About Page and using the provided About Page template, fill in the information that needs to be added or edited from your page.

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9 Module 3 - Begin with Your Start Here Page  ü Your Start Page is the portal to everything else your site has to offer ü It will lead visitors to your end goal ü The main purpose is to state who you are and to connect your visitor with the page they need  Start Page Content Must-Haves Clarity ü It should welcome and clearly tell people where to go Your Objectives ü Tell visitors what to expect Your Target ü Set expectations and describe who the site is for About Your Visitor ü Make it all about the visitor Logical Organization ü Make it flow logically and naturally Call to Action ü Tell them what they need to do

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10 Tips for Creating an Effective Start Here Page ü Use multimedia, like an introductory video ü Use social proof ü Show off your best content ü Don’t duplicate too much from the About Us page ü The sole function is to help visitors    Action Steps: 1. Using the provided outline, document what you need the user to understand so they will comfortably navigate to other pages on your website based on what they’re looking for.  Here are questions to help you outline your Start Here page (you don't need to include all): ü Who is this site for? ü What is this page specifically for? ü What will your user gain from the site? ü Who are you? ü What can people expect? ü What is some of the most popular content for visitors to look at first? ü How can users find you? ü How can users contact you? ü What are your most popular or important services? 2. List 3 Calls to Action that would benefit the customer and move them further along the sales cycle and engage them more on your website. Note where you will put the calls to action on your Start Here page.

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11 Module 4 - Create a Magnetic Blog That Keeps Readers Coming Back  ü Provide content that will engage and get visitors to read more ü Build reputation for expertise ü Regular posting will bring more traffic to your site  What is a Blog Page and Why is it Important? ü Most recent and archived posts ü Serves as a repository for all of your knowledge and expertise ü Allows your site to grow ü Establish yourself as a thought leader through content ü SEO benefits ü Use as part of your backlinking strategy  Why You Might Not Want a Blog Page on Your Website ü Better to have no blog than a bad blog ü Reasons for no blog include: o You can’t update regularly o You can’t write it o It doesn’t offer anything new or original o The tone doesn’t match the site o It’s overly promotional ü You may maintain a blog elsewhere

PAGE_12:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 12 Elements to Include on Your Blog Page Title and Headline ü Describe benefits of reading the blog ü Have a title and a headline that clearly describe you and your blog  Your Profile ü There should be a profile of you or the writer of your blog ü The bio should give some personal details and also explain the writer's expertise  Call to Action ü If you don't include one, you're missing out on a great opportunity  Categories ü Tags make your posts searchable ü Categories and tags make it easier for visitors to find the topics they're looking for  Comments ü It allows your readers to get involved ü It also gives you a direct line of communication with them  Other things to Include ü Social media buttons ü ‘Join me on’ social media links ü Subscription form

PAGE_13:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 13 ü Social proof ü Information on products and services ü Contact form  Your Blog Page Style Guide ü Cover topics that are interesting to your visitors ü Consider common questions ü Blog about your company or products/services ü Incorporate relevant keywords ü Use keywords in titles and headers ü Write small paragraphs with headers ü Use large fonts and easy to read colors    Action Steps: 1. After reviewing the module, determine if you should have a blog page on your website and if you do, draft an outline of the components you’ll include on the main Blog Page. 2. If you already have a blog on your site, review it based on the guidelines in this module and note where you need to add or make changes.

PAGE_14:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 14 Module 5 - Additional Critical Website Pages to Include  ü There are a few other critical pages every site should have, particularly business sites  Contact Us ü Sole purpose is to give an easy way to contact you ü Having it there builds trust ü Be ready to respond ü Wording should be concise and professional ü Tell visitors how long it will take you to respond ü Test your page and make sure it works  Site Map ü An index or directory that lists all of the pages ü Describes basic
